synopsis: Redundancy earns safety credit only when a single cause cannot disable both channels; shared power, software bugs, environmental stresses, assumptions or calibration errors can defeat apparent independence [f12112, f12113, f12114]. Achieved Performance Level depends partly on common-cause protection, and ISO 13849 scores defenses including separation, diverse technologies and environmental protection; the glossary identifies diversity as the strongest defense discussed [f12025, f12115, f12116]. Sensor fusion therefore requires evidence addressing correlated degradation and disagreement between modalities, including physical evidence for environmental contrast, contamination and calibration [f505, f506, f12117]. Across planning and skeptical review, the booklet warns that shared assumptions in the product, virtual sensors, collision logic and test oracle can yield consistent but misleading results; independent real-world referents and validation sources that do not share simulator assumptions are the proposed defenses [f10344, f10606, f11245, f11247, f12123]. This virtual-testing risk is an inference from standard verification and validation practice: no documented off-road collision-system case producing misleading virtual results, or off-road accident attributed to a product–test-environment common-mode error, was found [f10607, f11246].
